problem: The claim "16-QAM at the same E_s as QPSK has 6 dB less energy per bit, since E_s = 4E_b" is wrong. At the same E_s, QPSK gives E_b = E_s/2 and 16-QAM gives E_b = E_s/4, so 16-QAM has only half the energy per bit, i.e. 3 dB less than QPSK, not 6 dB. The 6 dB figure is the comparison against BPSK (E_s = E_b), not QPSK.
fix: 16-QAM at the same E_s as QPSK has 3 dB less energy per bit, because E_s = 2E_b for QPSK but E_s = 4E_b for 16-QAM, so E_b halves; its P_b is far worse. The 6 dB figure applies only when 16-QAM is compared with BPSK at the same E_s.

problem: The caption says the nearest-neighbour spacing shrinks as more points are packed into the same energy, but all three constellations are drawn on the same scale, so the spacing is 2 in every case (BPSK ±1, QPSK (±1, ±1), 16-QAM levels ±1, ±3). The average energies actually plotted are 1, 2 and 10, so the picture does not show what the caption claims.
fix: Either reword the caption to "the 16-QAM grid extends to ±3a while BPSK points sit at ±√E_b, so for equal average energy the 16-QAM points would be much closer together", or rescale each constellation to the same average energy so the spacing really does shrink.

problem: "About 4 dB at each step" is accurate for QPSK to 16-QAM (4/1.6 = 2.5, i.e. 4 dB) but the second step is 1.6/0.57 = 2.8, which is 4.5 dB.
fix: Write "about 4 dB from QPSK to 16-QAM and about 4.5 dB from 16-QAM to 64-QAM" so the numbers match the d_min² values quoted.
